name: base
title: Maths and general science
summary: SAT, SMT and optimisation solvers, computer algebra, graph generation, exact and numerical Python, and light libraries for chemistry, biology and astronomy.

tools.name: kissat
tools.does: SAT solver, usually the fastest here; can write a proof of unsatisfiability
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; kissat -q t.cnf; true

tools.name: cadical
tools.does: SAT solver
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; cadical -q t.cnf; true

tools.name: minisat
tools.does: SAT solver, small and classic
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; minisat t.cnf out >/dev/null 2>&1; cat out

tools.name: drat-trim
tools.does: checks a SAT solver's proof of unsatisfiability, independently of the solver
tools.usage: kissat FILE.cnf PROOF.drat; drat-trim FILE.cnf PROOF.drat
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 2 4
1 2 0
-1 2 0
1 -2 0
-1 -2 0
' > t.cnf; kissat -q t.cnf t.drat >/dev/null; drat-trim t.cnf t.drat

tools.name: pysat
tools.does: SAT solvers from Python (CaDiCaL, Glucose and others), with encodings for cardinality constraints
tools.usage: python: from pysat.solvers import Cadical153; from pysat.formula import CNF; from pysat.card import CardEnc
tools.check: python -c "from pysat.solvers import Cadical153; s=Cadical153(bootstrap_with=[[1],[-1]]); print('answer', 'sat' if s.solve() else 'unsat')"

tools.name: z3
tools.does: SMT solver: integers, reals, bit-vectors, arrays, quantifiers
tools.check: python -c "import z3; x=z3.Int('x'); s=z3.Solver(); s.add(x*x==49, x>0); print(s.check(), s.model()[x])"

tools.name: ortools
tools.does: CP-SAT: constraint and integer programming, good at scheduling and combinatorial search
tools.check: python -c "from ortools.sat.python import cp_model as c; m=c.CpModel(); x=m.NewIntVar(0,10,'x'); m.Add(2*x==14); s=c.CpSolver(); s.Solve(m); print('x =', s.Value(x))"

tools.name: highs
tools.does: linear and mixed-integer programming (HiGHS). Use it in a script of its own: it cannot be loaded together with ortools
tools.check: python -c "import highspy; print('highs', type(highspy.Highs()).__name__)"

tools.name: scip
tools.does: global mixed-integer nonlinear optimisation, with a proof of optimality
tools.check: python -c "from pyscipopt import Model; m=Model(); m.hideOutput(); x=m.addVar(lb=0,ub=4); m.setObjective(x,'maximize'); m.optimize(); print('best', m.getObjVal())"

tools.name: pari-gp
tools.does: number theory: factoring, primality, number fields, elliptic curves, modular forms
tools.check: echo 'print(factor(2^64+1))' | gp -q

tools.name: gap
tools.does: group theory and discrete algebra (core packages)
tools.check: printf '%s\n' 'Print(Size(SymmetricGroup(5)));' | gap -q

tools.name: singular
tools.does: commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: Gröbner bases, ideals, resolutions
tools.check: echo 'ring r=0,(x,y),dp; ideal i=x2+y2-1,x-y; print(std(i)); quit;' | Singular -q

tools.name: nauty
tools.does: generates graphs up to isomorphism and computes canonical forms and automorphism groups
tools.usage: geng -c N   |   genbg, labelg, shortg, countg   |   python: import pynauty
tools.check: geng -c 5 2>/dev/null | wc -l

tools.name: networkx
tools.does: graph algorithms in Python
tools.check: python -c "import networkx as nx; print('petersen', nx.petersen_graph().number_of_edges())"

tools.name: sympy
tools.does: symbolic mathematics: algebra, calculus, exact arithmetic
tools.check: python -c "import sympy; print(sympy.factorint(2**32+1))"

tools.name: flint and mpmath
tools.does: fast exact arithmetic on integers and polynomials (flint); arbitrary-precision real and complex numbers (mpmath)
tools.check: python -c "import flint, mpmath; mpmath.mp.dps=30; print(flint.fmpz(2)**100, mpmath.zeta(2))"

tools.name: numpy stack
tools.does: numerical computing, data frames, statistics, machine learning and plots (plots are saved to files; there is no display)
tools.usage: python: numpy, scipy, pandas, statsmodels, sklearn, matplotlib
tools.check: python -c "import numpy, scipy, pandas, statsmodels, sklearn, matplotlib; print('stack ok', numpy.linalg.det(numpy.eye(3)))"

tools.name: rdkit
tools.does: cheminformatics: molecules from SMILES, descriptors, substructure search, conformers
tools.check: python -c "from rdkit import Chem; print('atoms', Chem.MolFromSmiles('CCO').GetNumAtoms())"

tools.name: biopython
tools.does: sequences, alignments and common bioinformatics file formats
tools.check: python -c "from Bio.Seq import Seq; print(Seq('ATGC').reverse_complement())"

tools.name: astropy
tools.does: astronomy: units, coordinates, time, FITS files, cosmology
tools.check: python -c "import astropy.units as u; print((1*u.pc).to(u.lyr))"

tools.name: data file readers
tools.does: reads SPSS, Stata and SAS files (pyreadstat) and R .rds and .RData files (pyreadr)
tools.check: python -c "import pyreadstat, pyreadr; print('readers ok')"

tools.name: pdf tools
tools.does: turns PDFs into text
tools.usage: pdftotext -layout FILE.pdf OUT.txt   |   pdfinfo FILE.pdf   |   python: import pypdf
tools.check: pdftotext -v 2>&1 | head -1; python -c "import pypdf; print('pypdf ok')"
